problem: VLN agents trained on a few Matterport3D houses (61 training scans) overfit seen environments and generalize poorly to unseen ones. Prior agents are also trained on one task at a time (e.g., R2R instruction following or CVDN Navigation-from-Dialog-History), so a new agent must be trained from scratch for each task, and data for any single task stays scarce.
motivation: Human language annotations and scanned houses are expensive and limited by privacy, so data cannot be scaled by exhaustive sampling as in vision-only navigation. VLN (step-by-step instructions) and NDH (dialog to reach a goal room) use the same environments and action space. The authors observe that seen-unseen gaps partly come from house-specific features. They argue that sharing data across tasks and removing environment identity from the representation should improve unseen generalization.
key_idea: Train one RCM-style agent jointly on VLN (R2R) and NDH (CVDN) with interleaved batches and fully shared parameters. Attach a house-ID classifier behind a gradient reversal layer so the trajectory encoder learns environment-agnostic representations.
insight: The environment-aware ablation in Table 5 isolates the adversarial effect. Removing the gradient reversal layer so that the encoder learns to predict the house raises seen performance (VLN val-seen SR 57.59, NDH seen progress 8.38) but hurts unseen performance (VLN val-unseen SR 38.83, NDH unseen 1.81). EnvAg gives 44.40 SR and 3.15 progress. t-SNE shows environment-aware features cluster by house, which is direct evidence of house-specific overfitting. For multitask learning: VLN consistently helps NDH. NDH helps VLN only when richer dialog history is given (target-object-only gives 42.75 vs 42.93 single-task SR; full dialog gives 46.20). A shared language encoder beats separate encoders (46.20 vs 43.64 VLN unseen SR). With total training paths fixed at 4,742, mixing in 30% VLN paths still raises NDH unseen progress from 2.64 to 3.31, so the gain is not only extra data. A room-distance reward for NDH beats a goal-location reward. The two techniques are complementary on SR and progress, but EnvAg lowers SPL in the multitask setting (41.80 vs 44.19).
method: Shared RCM agent: randomly initialized word embeddings, 2-layer BiLSTM language encoder (256 per direction) over the union vocabulary of both tasks, and 2-layer LSTM trajectory encoder (512) over attention-pooled 36-view panoramic CNN features plus orientation. CM-ATT textual/visual attention and a bilinear action predictor over navigable directions; all parameters are shared between VLN and NDH.
Interleaved multitask data sampling: each mini-batch mixes R2R instruction-trajectory pairs and CVDN dialog-trajectory pairs, to avoid overfitting either task.

Task-specific reward shaping: dense reward for reduction in distance to goal, plus a terminal success indicator. For NDH the distance is the minimum distance to any node of the goal room (room navigation rather than point navigation).
Mixed navigation loss: REINFORCE with a baseline plus behavior cloning on human-demonstrated actions. NDH uses mixed supervision (navigator or oracle path as ground truth, following Thomason et al.).

Environment-agnostic learning: a 2-layer MLP classifier predicts the house ID from the trajectory encoder state h_t^V. A gradient reversal layer (λ=1.3) makes the encoder maximize the classification loss while minimizing the navigation loss (adversarial, DANN-style).
Distributed actor-learner training with VALAN (IMPALA/V-trace style) on TensorFlow.

setting.backbone: RCM-style LSTM encoders + cross-modal attention on pre-trained CNN image features (trained from scratch)

results: On R2R val-unseen, MT-RCM + EnvAg reaches 47.22 SR / 41.80 SPL, versus the equivalent RCM baseline's 40.6 SR (+16% relative) and its own single-task RCM's 42.93 SR. On CVDN/NDH val-unseen it reaches 4.65 m goal progress, versus the Seq2Seq baseline's 2.10 m (>120%). On the CVDN test leaderboard it scores 3.91 versus Seq2Seq's 2.35, a new state of the art (>66%). On the R2R test leaderboard it gets 45 SR / 40 SPL, beating RCM (43/38) but trailing augmentation- or pretraining-based methods such as EnvDrop (51/47) and PREVALENT (54/51). Both components shrink the seen-unseen gap; for example, multitask learning cuts the NDH progress gap from 3.85 m to 0.92 m.
limitations: Absolute R2R performance lags contemporary methods that use data augmentation or pre-training (EnvDrop, PREVALENT). The authors note these are complementary but do not combine them.
Environment-agnostic learning trades away seen-environment performance, and in the multitask setting it reduces SPL (41.80 vs 44.19 on R2R val-unseen) while slightly raising SR.

Evaluated only on two tasks that share the same Matterport3D houses and discrete nav-graph; the method needs house labels, and transfer to other domains (e.g., Touchdown) or continuous settings is left to future work.
